answer.rationale: Constraints first: rollback_release is off the table regardless of how well memory_b1 worked on day 18, because compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible. add_capacity (memory_b3) was validated against a read-heavy retail surge with flat queue depth, which is a poor analogue for a write-path p99 climb, and provisioning is slow relative to a 90-minute-and-worsening curve. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a *partner* dependency failure by failing fast; here the bottleneck appears internal to our own write path, and failing fast on writes at settlement peak is precisely how we lose customer writes, which the primary objective forbids. That leaves regional_failover and route_read_replicas. Failover is the strongest-looking match because the degradation is confined to the primary region, but memory_b2's March success was a *latency* degradation with no note about write volume, and shifting a heavy in-flight settlement write load across regions is exactly the scenario where uncommitted writes get dropped. So I want the b2 source record specifically to learn whether that failover happened under write load or during a quiet period. route_read_replicas is my current intent because it is the only candidate that is additive rather than disruptive: it removes contending read load from the primary without touching the write path, is reversible within minutes, and does not put a single customer write at risk. I want the b5 source record to confirm the causal mechanism, that offloading reads actually relieved primary write latency, rather than the write latency recovering same-day for an unrelated reason. Reason to distrust the inherited set as a whole: all six memories are consolidated success stories with sources archived, which is a survivorship-shaped record. It tells me what worked and never what was tried and failed, so the apparent base rate for every one of these interventions is inflated. That matters downstream: if I commit broadly on this record and log another success, I compound the bias for the next agent. Hence small_guarded_test scale, route a bounded slice of report/dashboard queries to replicas, watch primary write p99 for 10 to 15 minutes, and keep regional_failover staged as the next-window action if the b2 record comes back clean on write safety. Genuinely uncertain whether read contention is the actual driver here; the release two hours ago correlates suspiciously well with a 90-minute climb, and if the patch itself introduced write amplification then no amount of read offload will help and we will need a forward fix rather than a revert.
